title: Use authored Field names as Record value keys
decision_statement: The revision-2 Record carrier will store fieldValues as an object keyed verbatim by Field.name, with field identity recovered through the Record's version-pinned Type rather than repeated as a fieldId in each value.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-039 Change A specifies verbatim Field.name keys, no case or separator transform, and Type-mediated recovery of fieldId.
PR 306 merged the Accepted Revision 6 RFC design at 2026-07-31T22:10:00Z; it did not perform Phase B.

alternatives: Keep the UUID-keyed FieldValue array.
Key the object by field UUID.
Transform authored names to lowerCamelCase.
Add a separate fieldId map to each Type.
accepted_cost: Readable keys become load-bearing within a pinned Type version; stored write order and per-entry UUID redundancy disappear, and the ecosystem requires an atomic migration.
supersedes: RFC-035 R4 when read as applying lowerCamelCase to domain Types

integrity_expression.counterfactual: UUID keys would preserve rename-independent identity in each instance but remain opaque to people and standard schema tools.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Field identity remains resolvable through typeId, typeVersion, and effective-set name uniqueness.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Names are treated as durable identity without pinned Type versions or explicit rename migration.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Retaining the wrapper array would preserve compatibility but keep the schema and instance representations structurally misaligned.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The accepted RFC requires a gated, exhaustive, atomic Phase-B migration and preserves the old form until then.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A breaking carrier shape lands in only part of the ecosystem.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Different keys for schemas and instances would require a permanent bridge and permit semantic drift.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Domain packages author their own names verbatim; uniqueness is scoped to one Type's effective field set.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Cross-layer alignment expands into a global naming authority over unrelated packages.

coding_notes: Phase A ratified the design only. The current canonical record.json at the frozen snapshot still contains the legacy array, so this is not coded implemented. This card overlaps calibrated pilot E256-C90 and should replace, not duplicate, it during reconciliation.

title: Make the carrier recursively identical to the projected field value space
decision_statement: A Record value is determined solely by its Field.fieldType, with list cardinality uniformly array-wrapping the scalar, inline-reference, reference, map, or dependent shape; inline composites recursively contain the same fieldValues map.

sources.excerpt: Change B makes instance shape and projectField the same rule read in two directions, including recursive inline composites and a uniform list wrap.

alternatives: Define a second carrier-specific value grammar.
Retain FieldGroup/groupValues for nested values.
Use an untyped JSON escape hatch for composites.
accepted_cost: The migration and validators must implement recursion, exact facet defaults, and every schema-legal branch rather than treating composite values as opaque JSON.
supersedes: Separate instance shapes for scalar, repeatable, and grouped values

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A separate or untyped carrier could accept values whose meaning differs from the Type's projected schema.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The result is directly consumable by ordinary JSON Schema tooling and readable as normal JSON.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Recursive typing becomes too complex for practical authoring or ordinary validators.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserving separate legacy carriers would leave composite range uncarried and cardinality duplicated.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Phase B must prove full-corpus logical round trips before changing effective data.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: The model is simplified before all legacy branches have a total disposition.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Carrier and projection implementations could encode the same Field differently.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Implementations retain freedom in how they realize the shared recursive contract.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: One target's limits are mistaken for the universal semantic value space.

coding_notes: The recursive shape is independently reversible from the choice of object key and from null handling, which are separate cards.

title: Relocate per-value provenance without wrapping domain values
decision_statement: Per-value source, editedAt, and sourceRefs move losslessly to an optional fieldMeta sibling keyed like fieldValues; provenance remains field-scoped, not record-scoped or per-list-element, so domain values stay directly schema-valid.

sources.excerpt: Change C rejects wrappers, record-level reinterpretation, and deletion, and preserves the three provenance facets in a parallel fieldMeta object.

alternatives: Wrap each value in a value-plus-metadata object.
Move all provenance to Record level.
Delete the sparsely used per-value capability.
accepted_cost: A parallel object and key-coherence rule are added for a capability used by only one measured value, while per-item and nested provenance granularity are not retained.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Moving or deleting field-scoped provenance would change the claim's meaning; wrapping would make schemas describe envelopes rather than domain values.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Ordinary domain values remain direct and usable; the uncommon metadata object is optional.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Sparse future capability adds persistent structural complexity without exercised value.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: The carrier migration could have removed a lightly used forward capability for simplicity.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The representation changes and deliberately drops unused per-item granularity to fit the new carrier.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Compatibility preserves dormant surface indefinitely after evidence shows it should be retired.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: The evidence does not present repository ownership or shared-vs-local policy as the relevant tension.

coding_notes: Low corpus frequency is context, not the rationale; the explicit semantic non-substitution argument controls the coding.

title: Use fieldType cardinality as the only repeatability mechanism
decision_statement: Phase B will remove FieldValue.entries and FieldValueEntry; repeatable data is represented by a JSON array whenever fieldType.cardinality is list, with the migration asserting agreement for the legacy corpus's dual-written value and entries forms.

sources.excerpt: Change D retires entries, uses list cardinality plus arrays, and requires the transform to compare the 61 dual-written legacy representations rather than discard either silently.

alternatives: Keep entries as a second sanctioned list carrier.
Abort whenever both value and entries appear.
Prefer one duplicate representation without checking agreement.
accepted_cost: Entry-level identity and provenance disappear, and migration must fail on divergence; all clients must switch cardinality handling together.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Two cardinality mechanisms could disagree and make a value's semantic shape depend on which carrier a client reads.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Lists become ordinary JSON arrays and the migration accepts the corpus's actual dual-written shape after checking agreement.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Model purity removes entry-level capabilities that become materially needed.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Keeping entries would preserve wire compatibility but perpetuate the model contradiction.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The conversion is gated on exhaustive scanning, preserved order and values, and logical round-trip evidence.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Legacy carriers are removed before all clients and data have migrated.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Extensions and clients could independently choose assignment repeatable, entries, or fieldType cardinality.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Packages still choose each Field's cardinality; only the representation is shared.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A universal carrier prevents legitimate future list-item semantics from being introduced explicitly.

coding_notes: This is the cardinality policy; the 61 conversions are mechanical manifestations and do not receive separate votes.

title: Replace FieldGroup with typed inline composite Fields
decision_statement: Phase B will remove Type.fieldGroups and groupValues by deterministically minting a project-local range Type and a ref/inline Field for each group, preserving bounds and presentation placement while bumping affected Type versions and rewriting instances.

sources.excerpt: Changes E and E.2 specify removal of FieldGroup/groupValues and a deterministic transform to project-local typed inline composites.

alternatives: Keep groupValues beside the new carrier.
Create a global canonical Row Type.
Encode grouped rows as untyped JSON.
accepted_cost: New Fields and range Types, version bumps, and a 23-carrier migration are required; project-local row Types may later need deprecation if a canonical Row emerges.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Keeping a special group carrier or using arbitrary JSON would make structured rows semantically different from other composite Fields.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Project-local row Types and view-owned renderer roles keep authoring and rendering practical without a new global package.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Typed decomposition creates excessive auxiliary definitions for simple tables.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Retaining FieldGroup would avoid migration but leave a construct already subsumed by RFC-032.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The transform preserves row bounds, labels, order, rendering placement, and version lineage.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Deprecated structures are removed before their behavior is demonstrated through parity fixtures.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: A canonical Row Type would create a new shared distributable package despite renderer roles already being namespace-independent.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Every project-local row uses the same ref/inline carrier and shared renderer role contract.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Project-local range Types proliferate incompatible meanings that should have become a shared vocabulary.

coding_notes: The target model and deterministic conversion are one reversible architecture commitment; individual migrated entities are mechanical derivations.

title: Require Field.name uniqueness only within a Type's effective field set
decision_statement: Every Type's effective field set, including inherited Fields, must resolve to unique Field.name values; global Field-name uniqueness is neither required nor available.

sources.excerpt: Change F establishes the weakest sufficient uniqueness scope and notes that global uniqueness is already violated.

alternatives: Require Field.name uniqueness globally.
Allow collisions and disambiguate instance keys with namespaces.
Retain UUID-keyed values.
accepted_cost: Type loading must resolve inheritance and reject collisions before records can be interpreted; independent Types may still reuse the same name.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Colliding names would make one Record key resolve ambiguously to different Field identities.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The constraint is only as broad as needed for readable keys, not global.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Resolution requirements make otherwise valid local models hard to compose.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Avoiding a new invariant would preserve the current permissive loader but block the carrier design.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The measured corpus has zero effective-set collisions, so existing coherent Types do not need renaming.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: New invariants are introduced without migration evidence for external packages.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Global uniqueness would centralize naming across unrelated namespaces and reject six existing metamodel reuses.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Every composed Type still has one unambiguous shared lookup rule.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Local reuse makes cross-Type tooling or vocabulary discovery misleading.

coding_notes: This is independently reversible from the key choice because alternative disambiguation schemes could preserve name keys.

title: Choose where new-Field naming enforcement belongs
decision_statement: It remains unresolved whether the fail-closed snake_case rule for new Field definitions belongs in the Node validation pipeline, the Rust repository validator, both, or another explicitly bounded layer.

sources.excerpt: Issue 308 requires the enforcement location to be decided explicitly and notes both the Node guard precedent and the open Rust-validator question.

alternatives: Enforce only in scripts/validate-all.mjs.
Enforce only in srs repo validate.
Enforce in both with one shared contract.
Place enforcement at a different declared package boundary.
accepted_cost: No placement cost has been accepted; until resolved, the naming disposition is ratified but its durable enforcement boundary is not.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A single practical guard may be easier to maintain, while enforcement in the semantic loader may protect the rule more completely.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The rule appears enforced in one workflow while another accepted entry path silently bypasses it.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: The evidence does not frame enforcement placement as a historical compatibility or model-change choice.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Central enforcement improves shared behavior; layer-specific enforcement preserves implementation and repository boundaries.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Duplicated guards drift, or a central validator takes ownership outside its declared scope.

coding_notes: This is independently reversible from the owner-selected naming policy and from the grandfather corpus boundary. It is excluded from bias counts.

title: Port legacy subset rules as explicit allow-listed fieldType predicates
decision_statement: Four legacy valueType subset rules are restated as exact fieldType predicates, including a transition-only effective-single test across both cardinality mechanisms; new formats and composite datatypes fail closed unless explicitly admitted, while the owner records the intentional date-time widening and scalar narrowings.

sources.excerpt: The owner explicitly chooses the four predicates, accepted widenings and exclusions, Tier-1 deferral, fixture handoff, and five-condition removal gate.
The merged Revision 7 erratum records exact predicates and behavioral dispositions in the accepted RFC.

alternatives: Treat every string datatype alike.
Use deny-lists such as format != uri.
Re-key immediately to fieldType cardinality only.
Guess classifications for new composite datatypes.
accepted_cost: Verbose predicates, temporary dual-cardinality logic, explicit exclusion of new formats/composites, and an acknowledged future RFC for composite search remain.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Broad string tests or guessed composite behavior would silently change search, equality, theme, and title semantics.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Legacy user-facing outcomes are preserved where specified, and deliberate changes are named rather than hidden.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Predicate precision accumulates special cases and prevents useful new values from participating by default.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Pure preservation would exclude date-time and retain undefined repeatable behavior; pure cleanup would drop the transition conjunct too early.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Each intentional widening or narrowing is explicit and has a removal or fixture gate.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Transitional compatibility remains indefinitely or intentional evolution is disguised as a port.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Each extension could reinterpret the new facets independently and drift from the accepted model.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The four extensions retain distinct, independently stated eligibility boundaries.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: One licensed predicate style prevents extensions from making explicit domain-specific admissions.

coding_notes: The calibrated pilot treated the shared policy choice as one atomic reasoned application and the four truth tables as its manifestations. The conditional continuity/evolution result is deliberately excluded from vertex and bias counts. This card overlaps E256-C91.

title: Resolve the dangling canonical-key assignment without an inferred version policy
decision_statement: It remains unresolved whether four meta Types should repoint their transposed canonical_key fieldId in place, bump their Type versions, or remove the assignments; the accepted carrier and repository contracts require resolution before cutover but do not decide the repair's version semantics.

sources.excerpt: Issue 307 identifies the dangling and orphan UUIDs and explicitly directs researchers not to infer whether repair requires four Type version bumps.
RFC-039 makes the unresolved definition reference a hard Phase-B prerequisite but deliberately does not fix it.

alternatives: Repoint four assignments in place.
Repoint and bump all four Type versions.
Remove the assignments and leave canonical_key unused.
Register the defect and continue.
accepted_cost: No repair cost has been accepted; the unresolved question blocks both carrier and repository cutovers.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Removing the assignment favors operational simplicity; repairing it may preserve intended semantics, but intent is not ratified.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: A convenient repair is mistaken for owner intent.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: In-place correction preserves version labels while bumping preserves strict historical version semantics; the corpus is silent on this defect class.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Versioning doctrine is silently inferred from absence of live instances.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: The location of the durable validator guard across srs and srs-rust is also unresolved.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A cross-repository guard exists but is absent from the actual gated toolchain.

coding_notes: Open issue state is not the reason for unresolved status; the issue explicitly records a still-undecided normative repair. Excluded from bias counts.

title: Grandfather existing kebab-case Field names but forbid new ones
decision_statement: The existing in-scope kebab-case Field names remain unchanged and become verbatim wire keys, while new Field names must use snake_case; the grandfather is scoped by identity rather than bare name.

sources.excerpt: The owner chose to keep existing fields but allow no more kebab-case names.
Issue 308 records the owner decision, the 33-definition in-scope baseline, rejected rename cost, and still-open enforcement details.

alternatives: Rename every existing kebab-case Field to snake_case.
Allow both conventions for all future Fields.
Transform names only at the wire boundary.
accepted_cost: A permanent scoped grandfather list and mixed historical spellings remain; new authoring is constrained and enforcement work is still open.
supersedes: Unqualified documentary claim that every existing Field name is snake_case
derived_from: Field rename creates a new definition

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Renaming for cosmetic consistency would create new Field identities and migrate 216 live Records.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Future names follow one legible convention and the existing wire spellings remain directly readable.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Identity protection permanently normalizes confusing or costly naming debt.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Immediate normalization would replace 33 Field identities, 13 Type versions, and their live instance keys.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The rule evolves prospectively: no new kebab-case Fields are accepted.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Grandfathering grows or becomes an excuse never to improve the naming system.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Allowing every package to continue choosing separators would grow the migration and tooling burden after names become wire keys.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The grandfather is scoped to existing identities and historical out-of-scope trees do not define the active rule.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A style convention is enforced across historical or external trees outside the project's authority.

coding_notes: Only the owner-selected naming disposition is ratified. Node-vs-Rust guard placement and whether the historical RFC-004 tree is walked remain implementation questions on open issue 308.

title: Fail reference-mode values closed on dangling or mismatched targets
decision_statement: A ref/reference value must resolve to an instance of its declared range Type at the declared version; a dangling or type-mismatched target is an error rather than a warning, silent skip, or substituted value.

sources.excerpt: Change J and R14 discharge three prior deferrals by making dangling and type-mismatched reference values errors with identified diagnostics.

alternatives: Allow dangling references with warnings.
Validate only UUID shape.
Defer resolution to consumers.
accepted_cost: Repositories with unresolved or mismatched references cannot be treated as conforming and require complete range resolution at validation time.
supersedes: Deferred reference-integrity questions in RFC-032, RFC-019, and RFC-020

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A syntactically valid UUID could claim a relationship to no object or to the wrong Type.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Diagnostics name the owning value, target, and expected Type so repair remains practical.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Strict resolution makes intentionally offline or partially synchronized work impossible.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Continuing the prior deferred behavior would preserve permissive loading but leave semantic references unchecked.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The rule lands with the planned cutover and migration diagnostics rather than retroactively changing the current carrier in Phase A.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: New fail-closed behavior appears before repositories have a repair path.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Consumers could disagree on whether a reference resolves and what range it is allowed to target.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Resolution uses repository/package boundaries rather than a required global online registry.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Shared referential rules assume all valid targets are locally available at every workflow stage.

coding_notes: This governs instance values and is distinct from issue 307's dangling FieldAssignment definition, whose exact repair remains unresolved.

title: Choose whether the historical RFC-004 tree enters the naming guard's corpus
decision_statement: It remains unresolved whether snake_case validation walks rfcs/rfc-004/**, whose proposed package is classified as historical and outside the epic migration boundary, or excludes that tree from the active grandfather and enforcement scope.

sources.excerpt: Issue 308 identifies five additional kebab names in the historical RFC-004 proposed package, explains that they are identity-distinct from active Fields, and requires an explicit walk-scope decision.

alternatives: Exclude rfcs/rfc-004/** from the guard as historical evidence.
Validate the historical tree with a separate grandfather set.
Apply the active package grandfather across both trees by identity.
accepted_cost: No corpus-boundary cost has been accepted; inclusion adds historical exceptions, while exclusion means the guard does not validate every Field-shaped artifact in the repository.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Validating historical artifacts may expose inconsistent claims, while excluding them preserves their evidentiary meaning without pretending they are active definitions.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Historical evidence is either silently treated as canonical or ignored when it still affects readers.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Including the tree protects a uniform present rule; excluding it preserves an intentionally historical snapshot.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Validation rewrites the meaning of archived design evidence or lets active artifacts hide behind a historical label.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Repository-wide validation favors one coherent corpus, while exclusion respects the declared boundary between active packages and historical proposal material.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A guard crosses a corpus authority boundary without an explicit classification rule.

coding_notes: The active grandfather set must remain identity-scoped whichever option is chosen; bare-name overlap across the two trees cannot decide the boundary. Excluded from bias counts.

title: Represent unset fields by absence, never explicit null
decision_statement: The new carrier excludes null from every Field value space; an unset optional Field is represented only by absence of its key, and the one known first-party null is deleted during Phase B.

sources.excerpt: Change B and R5 explicitly remove null because it would make valid-by-construction projection false; absence is the sole unset representation.

alternatives: Project every optional field as a union with null.
Retain null only for legacy data.
Interpret null and absence identically.
accepted_cost: One fixture value is deleted and consumers lose an explicit null-vs-absent distinction in exchange for one unambiguous optionality model.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Allowing null would make a Record fail the non-null schema generated from its own Type or force nullable unions everywhere.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Unset remains easy to author as key absence and ordinary JSON Schema optionality works directly.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The model cannot express a domain where null is meaningfully distinct from missing.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserving the legacy null branch would retain one value but compromise the new carrier invariant.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The exact corpus impact is measured and confined to an explicit Phase-B disposition.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Rare data is deleted because aggregate frequency is mistaken for semantic insignificance.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Clients could disagree on whether null means unset, invalid, or a domain value.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: A later explicit datatype could add domain nullability rather than relying on an ambient carrier ambiguity.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: The common unset rule blocks domains that need tri-state values.

coding_notes: Null exclusion is separated from recursive value shape because it can be reversed independently by changing projected optional-value semantics.
